role: The host's voice — speech recognition and synthesis for every surface that listens or speaks.

fields.label: Speaking voice
fields.description: The voice every surface on this host speaks in — Discord, and anything else that asks. The first two letters are the accent and the speaker — b British, a American, then f or m. They are listed best-first within each accent, and the gap is worth hearing: the ones at the top of each group were trained on hours of speech and the ones at the bottom on minutes, which is the difference between a voice that sounds like a person and one that sounds like a synthesiser.

fields.label: Recognition model
fields.description: The speech recognition model file. Without it nothing said out loud is understood.

fields.label: Recognise on the GPU
fields.description: Whether to recognise speech on the graphics card. Around forty times faster than the processor; a host without a usable card falls back on its own.

fields.label: Synthesis model
fields.description: The speech synthesis model file. Without it surfaces answer in text only.

fields.label: Synthesise on the GPU
fields.description: Whether to synthesise speech on the graphics card. Around eight times faster than the processor and worth roughly 700MB of video memory; a host without a usable card falls back on its own.

fields.label: Unload after
fields.description: How many minutes to stay loaded after the last thing said or heard. The models cost around 1.6GB of memory and a gigabyte of video memory, all of which comes back when this exits — but loading them again takes a few seconds, which the next person to speak waits for. Zero stays loaded until the host restarts.

fields.label: Control socket
fields.description: The unix socket other services reach this one on. It has to match the socket unit, so leave it alone unless you are moving both.
